knitr::opts_chunk$set(collapse = TRUE, comment = "#>")
library(nlmixr2lib)
library(PKNCA)
library(rxode2)
library(dplyr)

# Model and source

```{r model}
ui <- rxode2::rxode(readModelDb("Jung_2026_tacrolimus"))
```

* Citation: `r ui$reference`
* Description: `r ui$description`
* Article: <https://doi.org/10.3389/fphar.2026.1896778>

Jung 2026 fitted a one-compartment model to routine whole-blood tacrolimus
troughs in children younger than 36 months during the first 11 days after
liver transplantation for biliary atresia. The model's distinguishing feature
is its inter-occasion variability (IOV) on apparent clearance: each of six
postoperative occasions has its own estimated variance, from a CV of 123.8% on
postoperative day (POD) 2 down to 10.7% on POD 5-6 and back up to 38.8% on
POD 9-11. The paper then uses the model for model-informed precision dosing: a
closed-form steady-state dose for a 10 ng/mL target trough (Equation 6,
Table 7) and maximum a posteriori (MAP) Bayesian forecasting in four example
subjects (Table 8). Both are reproduced below.

# Population

92 recipients of a primary living- or deceased-donor liver transplant for
biliary atresia at Asan Medical Center Children's Hospital (Seoul) between
January 2010 and May 2023, all younger than 36 months at transplantation
(Jung 2026 Table 1). Median age 11.7 months (range 3.3-35.5), median weight
8.95 kg (4.3-14.4), 58.7% female. Subject-level median total bilirubin
2.30 mg/dL (0.80-10.60) and AST 68 U/L (26-461); individual records reached
29.0 mg/dL and 8,781 U/L. Oral tacrolimus was started twice daily on POD 1 at
0.0375 mg/kg per dose and then adjusted by trough monitoring. The analysis
used 731 whole-blood concentrations (ACMIA immunoassay, LLOQ 1.0 ng/mL)
collected through POD 11 and grouped into six pharmacokinetic occasions
(Table 2).

```{r population}
str(ui$population)
```

# Source trace

| Equation / parameter | Value | Source location |
|---|---|---|
| Structure: 1-compartment, first-order absorption and elimination | -- | Methods, Structural model |
| `lka` (ka, 1/h) | 4.5, held constant | Table 4; Methods (from Wang et al. 2019) |
| `lcl` (CL/F at TBIL 2 mg/dL, AST 60 U/L, L/h) | 4.85 | Table 4; Equation 9 |
| `lvc` (V/F at 12 months, L) | 123.9 | Table 4 (Equation 10 rounds to 124) |
| `e_tbili_cl` | -0.353 | Table 4 ('negative power' 0.353); Equation 9 |
| `e_ast_cl` | -0.106 | Table 4 ('negative power' 0.106); Equation 9 |
| `e_age_vc` | 0.16, held constant | Table 4; Equation 10; Supplementary Table S2 (0.156) |
| CL/F = TV(CL/F) * exp(eta_CL + eta_OCC) | -- | Equation 1 |
| V/F = TV(V/F) * exp(eta_V) | -- | Equation 2 |
| `etalcl`, `etalvc` variances | 0.319, 0.258 | Table 5 |
| `etalcl`-`etalvc` covariance | 0.7 * sqrt(0.319 * 0.258) = 0.2008 | Table 5 (r = 0.7) |
| `etaiov_cl_1` ... `etaiov_cl_6` | 0.929, 0.114, 0.034, 0.011, 0.044, 0.14 | Table 5 |
| Occasion definition (OCC 1-6 = POD 2, 3, 4, 5-6, 7-8, 9-11) | -- | Methods, Fixed effect and random effect; Table 2 |
| Residual W = sqrt(add^2 + prop^2 * IPRED^2) | -- | Equation 3 |
| `addSd` (ng/mL) | 1.37 | Table 4 |
| `propSd` (fraction) | 0.206 | Table 4 |
| Steady-state dose for a target trough | -- | Equation 6 |
| Superposition / steady-state trough fraction | -- | Supplementary Table S3, Equations ST3-1 to ST3-3 |

# Covariate-based dosing (Table 7)

Table 7 evaluates the final covariate model at the median total bilirubin
and AST of each occasion and gives the steady-state dose (q12h) that attains a
10 ng/mL trough by Equation 6. The model is solved below at those covariates,
first for the typical CL/F and V/F, then at steady state on the paper's
tabulated doses to read the trough back. Table 7 does not state the age used
for V/F; the reference age of 12 months is used here, which reproduces every
tabulated dose to 0.01 mg.

```{r table7}
table7 <- data.frame(
  OCC = 1:6,
  POD = c("2", "3", "4", "5-6", "7-8", "9-11"),
  tbili_mgdl = c(4.60, 4.35, 3.50, 2.80, 1.80, 1.20),
  AST = c(188, 112, 77, 72, 54, 45),
  cl_pub = c(3.21, 3.45, 3.88, 4.23, 5.09, 5.99),
  dose_pub = c(0.45, 0.49, 0.56, 0.62, 0.78, 0.96)
)

# Equation 6: dose (mg) giving a steady-state trough ctrough (ng/mL) over tau (h)
eq6_dose <- function(cl, v, ka = 4.5, tau = 12, ctrough = 10) {
  k <- cl / v
  ctrough * (ka - k) / ka /
    (exp(-k * tau) / (1 - exp(-k * tau)) - exp(-ka * tau) / (1 - exp(-ka * tau))) *
    v / 1000
}

mod_typ <- rxode2::zeroRe(ui)

# Steady-state dosing at the published dose; the observation at 12 h is the
# trough immediately before the next dose.
ev7 <- table7 |>
  dplyr::mutate(id = OCC, TBILI = tbili_mgdl * 17.1, AGE = 1) |>
  dplyr::select(id, OCC, TBILI, AST, AGE, dose_pub) |>
  dplyr::cross_join(data.frame(rec = c("dose", "obs"))) |>
  dplyr::mutate(
    time = ifelse(rec == "dose", 0, 12),
    amt = ifelse(rec == "dose", dose_pub, 0),
    evid = ifelse(rec == "dose", 1L, 0L),
    ss = ifelse(rec == "dose", 1L, 0L),
    ii = ifelse(rec == "dose", 12, 0),
    cmt = ifelse(rec == "dose", "depot", "central")
  ) |>
  dplyr::select(id, time, amt, evid, ss, ii, cmt, OCC, TBILI, AST, AGE)

sim7 <- rxode2::rxSolve(mod_typ, ev7,
  returnType = "data.frame",
  rtol = 1e-10, atol = 1e-12, ssRtol = 1e-10, ssAtol = 1e-12, maxsteps = 1e6
)

chk7 <- table7 |>
  dplyr::left_join(
    sim7 |> dplyr::select(id, cl, vc, Cc) |> dplyr::rename(OCC = id),
    by = "OCC"
  ) |>
  dplyr::mutate(dose_eq6 = eq6_dose(cl, vc))

chk7 |>
  dplyr::transmute(
    OCC, POD,
    `TBIL (mg/dL)` = tbili_mgdl, `AST (U/L)` = AST,
    `CL/F model (L/h)` = round(cl, 3), `CL/F Table 7` = cl_pub,
    `Dose Eq. 6 (mg)` = round(dose_eq6, 3), `Dose Table 7` = dose_pub,
    `Trough at Table 7 dose (ng/mL)` = round(Cc, 2)
  ) |>
  knitr::kable(caption = "Replicates Table 7 of Jung 2026.")

stopifnot(
  # CL/F: Table 7 rounds to 0.01 L/h; the printed 4.85 L/h is itself rounded
  # (see Assumptions), so allow 0.5%.
  all(abs(chk7$cl / chk7$cl_pub - 1) < 0.005),
  # Dose: Table 7 prints two decimals.
  all(abs(chk7$dose_eq6 - chk7$dose_pub) < 0.006),
  # The ODE solve at the printed dose returns the 10 ng/mL target trough,
  # within the two-decimal rounding of the dose (worst case 0.005 / 0.45 = 1.1%).
  all(abs(chk7$Cc / 10 - 1) < 0.015)
)
```

# Bayesian forecasting in four subjects (Table 8)

Table 8 gives, for four subjects, the covariates on POD 2, the
covariate-based typical CL/F, V/F and dose, the MAP random effects estimated
from the single POD 2 trough, and the dose recommended for the next occasion
with the occasion deviation reset to zero. Every derived row is a function of
the model and the tabulated covariates and random effects, so each is
recomputed here by solving the packaged model with the published etas
supplied as individual parameters. Doses are rounded to the nearest 0.05 mg
as in the paper.

```{r table8}
table8 <- data.frame(
  subject = c("T082", "T067", "T054", "T027"),
  age_months = c(16.5, 24.6, 9.4, 16.2),
  tbili_mgdl = c(1.9, 1.7, 4.5, 8.2),
  AST = c(94, 93, 188, 6656),
  eta_cl = c(0.212, 0.004, -0.413, -0.641),
  eta_v = c(0.128, 0.003, -0.449, -0.749),
  kappa1 = c(0.639, 0.007, -0.359, -0.330),
  cl_typ_pub = c(4.71, 4.91, 3.23, 1.79),
  v_typ_pub = c(130.4, 139.0, 119.2, 130.0),
  dose_cov_pub = c(0.70, 0.75, 0.45, 0.25),
  cl_pod2_pub = c(11.04, 4.96, 1.49, 0.68),
  v_ind_pub = c(148.2, 139.5, 76.1, 61.5),
  dev_pub = c(134, 1, -54, -62),
  cl_next_pub = c(5.82, 4.93, 2.14, 0.94),
  dose_next_pub = c(0.90, 0.75, 0.30, 0.10),
  change_pub = c(29, 0, -33, -60),
  trough_next_pub = c(10.2, 10.3, 9.9, 8.1)
)
round_005 <- function(x) round(x / 0.05) * 0.05

# One solve per scenario: typical (all etas 0), POD 2 individual (eta + kappa1
# on occasion 1), next occasion (eta only, occasion 2 with kappa reset to 0).
iov_zero <- setNames(as.list(rep(0, 6)), paste0("etaiov_cl_", 1:6))
solve_tab8 <- function(scenario, occ, dose) {
  ev <- table8 |>
    dplyr::mutate(id = dplyr::row_number()) |>
    dplyr::cross_join(data.frame(rec = c("dose", "obs"))) |>
    dplyr::mutate(
      time = ifelse(rec == "dose", 0, 12),
      amt = ifelse(rec == "dose", dose, 0),
      evid = ifelse(rec == "dose", 1L, 0L),
      ss = ifelse(rec == "dose", 1L, 0L),
      ii = ifelse(rec == "dose", 12, 0),
      cmt = ifelse(rec == "dose", "depot", "central"),
      OCC = occ, TBILI = tbili_mgdl * 17.1, AGE = age_months / 12
    ) |>
    dplyr::select(id, time, amt, evid, ss, ii, cmt, OCC, TBILI, AST, AGE)
  prm <- data.frame(id = seq_len(nrow(table8)), iov_zero) |>
    dplyr::mutate(etalcl = 0, etalvc = 0)
  if (scenario != "typical") {
    prm$etalcl <- table8$eta_cl
    prm$etalvc <- table8$eta_v
  }
  if (scenario == "pod2") prm$etaiov_cl_1 <- table8$kappa1
  rxode2::rxSolve(ui, ev,
    params = prm, returnType = "data.frame",
    rtol = 1e-10, atol = 1e-12, ssRtol = 1e-10, ssAtol = 1e-12, maxsteps = 1e6
  ) |>
    dplyr::filter(time == 12) |>
    dplyr::arrange(id)
}

typ <- solve_tab8("typical", occ = 1, dose = 1)
pod2 <- solve_tab8("pod2", occ = 1, dose = 1)
nxt_unit <- solve_tab8("next", occ = 2, dose = 1)

chk8 <- table8 |>
  dplyr::mutate(
    cl_typ = typ$cl, v_typ = typ$vc,
    dose_cov = round_005(eq6_dose(cl_typ, v_typ)),
    cl_pod2 = pod2$cl, v_ind = pod2$vc,
    dev = 100 * (cl_pod2 / cl_typ - 1),
    cl_next = nxt_unit$cl,
    dose_next = round_005(eq6_dose(cl_next, v_ind)),
    change = 100 * (dose_next / dose_cov - 1),
    # Linear model: the steady-state trough scales with dose, so the unit-dose
    # steady-state solve times the recommended dose is the predicted trough.
    trough_next = nxt_unit$Cc * dose_next
  )

chk8 |>
  dplyr::transmute(
    Subject = subject,
    `Typical CL/F (model / paper)` = sprintf("%.2f / %.2f", cl_typ, cl_typ_pub),
    `Typical V/F` = sprintf("%.1f / %.1f", v_typ, v_typ_pub),
    `Covariate dose (mg)` = sprintf("%.2f / %.2f", dose_cov, dose_cov_pub),
    `POD 2 CL/F` = sprintf("%.2f / %.2f", cl_pod2, cl_pod2_pub),
    `Individual V/F` = sprintf("%.1f / %.1f", v_ind, v_ind_pub),
    `Deviation (%)` = sprintf("%+.0f / %+.0f", dev, dev_pub),
    `Next-occasion CL/F` = sprintf("%.2f / %.2f", cl_next, cl_next_pub),
    `Recommended dose (mg)` = sprintf("%.2f / %.2f", dose_next, dose_next_pub),
    `Change (%)` = sprintf("%+.0f / %+.0f", change, change_pub),
    `Predicted trough (ng/mL)` = sprintf("%.1f / %.1f", trough_next, trough_next_pub)
  ) |>
  knitr::kable(caption = "Replicates Table 8 of Jung 2026 (model / paper).")

stopifnot(
  # Two-decimal CL/F rows: the larger of 0.5% and half a rounding unit.
  all(abs(chk8$cl_typ - chk8$cl_typ_pub) < pmax(0.005 * chk8$cl_typ_pub, 0.0051)),
  all(abs(chk8$cl_pod2 - chk8$cl_pod2_pub) < pmax(0.005 * chk8$cl_pod2_pub, 0.0051)),
  all(abs(chk8$cl_next - chk8$cl_next_pub) < pmax(0.005 * chk8$cl_next_pub, 0.0051)),
  # One-decimal V/F rows. The individual V/F also carries the 3-decimal
  # rounding of the published eta (up to 0.0005 on the log scale; T067 gives
  # 139.40 L against a printed 139.5 L).
  all(abs(chk8$v_typ - chk8$v_typ_pub) < 0.051),
  all(abs(chk8$v_ind - chk8$v_ind_pub) < 0.051 + 0.0005 * chk8$v_ind_pub),
  # Doses after rounding to 0.05 mg match exactly.
  all(abs(chk8$dose_cov - chk8$dose_cov_pub) < 1e-9),
  all(abs(chk8$dose_next - chk8$dose_next_pub) < 1e-9),
  all(abs(chk8$change - chk8$change_pub) < 0.51),
  all(abs(chk8$dev - chk8$dev_pub) < 0.6),
  all(abs(chk8$trough_next - chk8$trough_next_pub) < 0.051)
)
```

The table's "Predicted POD 2 trough under the administered dose" row
(3.4, 4.1, 3.1, 2.7 ng/mL) depends on each subject's actual dosing times on
POD 1, which the paper does not give; it is not recomputed here.

# Accumulation on POD 2 (Supplementary Table S3)

Supplementary Table S3 attributes the low POD 2 troughs to incomplete
accumulation: a median of 46% of the steady-state trough had been attained at
the first occasion. For a subject with the OCC 1 median covariates of Table 7,
dosed at 0 and 12 h and sampled at 24 h (two doses on POD 1, the POD 2 morning
trough), the packaged model gives the same fraction. Later occasions in that
table are medians over the actual, individually adjusted dosing histories and
are not reproducible without the data.

```{r accumulation}
acc_ev <- data.frame(
  id = 1L,
  time = c(0, 12, 24),
  amt = c(1, 1, 0),
  evid = c(1L, 1L, 0L),
  cmt = c("depot", "depot", "central"),
  OCC = 1, TBILI = 4.60 * 17.1, AST = 188, AGE = 1
)
acc_ss <- data.frame(
  id = 1L, time = c(0, 12), amt = c(1, 0), evid = c(1L, 0L),
  ss = c(1L, 0L), ii = c(12, 0), cmt = c("depot", "central"),
  OCC = 1, TBILI = 4.60 * 17.1, AST = 188, AGE = 1
)
c_pod2 <- rxode2::rxSolve(mod_typ, acc_ev, returnType = "data.frame")$Cc
c_ss <- rxode2::rxSolve(mod_typ, acc_ss,
  returnType = "data.frame",
  ssRtol = 1e-10, ssAtol = 1e-12, maxsteps = 1e6
)$Cc
frac_pod2 <- 100 * c_pod2 / c_ss
frac_pod2
# Table S3 prints 46% (integer).
stopifnot(abs(frac_pod2 - 46) < 1)
```

# Virtual cohort and occasion-wise simulation

A virtual cohort of 200 children is dosed per the institutional protocol,
0.0375 mg/kg twice daily from the morning of POD 1 (time 0) through POD 11,
without the trough-guided adjustment the real cohort received. Age is drawn
log-normally around the cohort median of 11.7 months and truncated to the
observed 3.3-35.5 months. Body weight, which only sets the mg/kg dose, is the
WHO median weight-for-age (sexes averaged) scaled by 0.95 so that the cohort
median lands near the observed 8.95 kg (children with biliary atresia are
smaller than the WHO reference), with 10% log-normal scatter and truncation
to 4.3-14.4 kg. Total bilirubin and AST follow the occasion medians of
Table 7, each subject carrying one log-normal multiplier for each marker
across all occasions.

Each record's occasion follows its postoperative day, with days running from
midnight: POD 1 runs from 8 h before the first dose, so the POD 2 morning
trough at 24 h falls on POD 2 and carries OCC 1.

```{r cohort}
rxode2::rxSetSeed(2026)
n_sub <- 200

# WHO Child Growth Standards median weight-for-age (kg), boys and girls
# averaged, at 0, 3, 6, 12, 18, 24 and 36 months.
who_age <- c(0, 3, 6, 12, 18, 24, 36)
who_wt <- c(3.3, 6.1, 7.6, 9.3, 10.6, 11.8, 14.0)

cohort <- data.frame(id = seq_len(n_sub)) |>
  dplyr::mutate(
    age_months = pmin(pmax(exp(rnorm(n_sub, log(11.7), 0.6)), 3.3), 35.5),
    WT = pmin(pmax(
      0.95 * approx(who_age, who_wt, xout = age_months)$y * exp(rnorm(n_sub, 0, 0.1)),
      4.3
    ), 14.4),
    f_tbili = exp(rnorm(n_sub, 0, 0.5)),
    f_ast = exp(rnorm(n_sub, 0, 0.6)),
    dose = 0.0375 * WT
  )

pod_occ <- c(1, 1, 2, 3, 4, 4, 5, 5, 6, 6, 6) # POD 1..11
pod_tbili <- table7$tbili_mgdl[pod_occ]
pod_ast <- table7$AST[pod_occ]

dose_times <- seq(0, 252, by = 12)
trough_times <- 24 * (2:11 - 1) - 0.01
obs_times <- sort(unique(c(seq(0, 252, by = 1), trough_times)))

ev_cohort <- dplyr::bind_rows(
  cohort |>
    dplyr::cross_join(data.frame(time = dose_times)) |>
    dplyr::mutate(amt = dose, evid = 1L, cmt = "depot"),
  cohort |>
    dplyr::cross_join(data.frame(time = obs_times)) |>
    dplyr::mutate(amt = 0, evid = 0L, cmt = "central")
) |>
  dplyr::mutate(
    POD = pmin(floor((time + 8) / 24) + 1, 11),
    OCC = pod_occ[POD],
    TBILI = pod_tbili[POD] * f_tbili * 17.1,
    AST = pod_ast[POD] * f_ast,
    AGE = age_months / 12
  ) |>
  dplyr::arrange(id, time, dplyr::desc(evid == 0L)) |>
  dplyr::select(id, time, amt, evid, cmt, OCC, POD, TBILI, AST, AGE, WT)

sim <- rxode2::rxSolve(ui, ev_cohort,
  returnType = "data.frame",
  keep = c("POD", "WT"), maxsteps = 1e6
)

c(
  median_wt_kg = median(cohort$WT),
  median_age_months = median(cohort$age_months),
  median_dose_mg = median(cohort$dose)
)
```

```{r troughs, fig.width = 7, fig.height = 4.5}
troughs <- sim |>
  dplyr::filter(abs(time - round(time)) > 1e-6) |>
  dplyr::mutate(POD = round(time / 24) + 1) |>
  dplyr::group_by(POD) |>
  dplyr::summarise(
    p05 = quantile(Cc, 0.05), p50 = quantile(Cc, 0.50), p95 = quantile(Cc, 0.95),
    .groups = "drop"
  )

obs_tab2 <- data.frame(
  POD = 2:11,
  obs_median = c(4.0, 7.55, 9.2, 9.7, 9.3, 8.9, 8.3, 8.3, 8.8, 8.2)
)

ggplot(troughs, aes(POD)) +
  geom_ribbon(aes(ymin = p05, ymax = p95), fill = "steelblue", alpha = 0.25) +
  geom_line(aes(y = p50), colour = "steelblue") +
  geom_point(data = obs_tab2, aes(y = obs_median), colour = "firebrick") +
  scale_y_log10() +
  scale_x_continuous(breaks = 2:11) +
  labs(
    x = "Postoperative day", y = "Morning trough (ng/mL)",
    caption = paste(
      "Band: 5th-95th percentile and median of the simulated individual",
      "predictions (no residual error) at the protocol dose.",
      "Red: observed median trough by day (Jung 2026 Table 2), after",
      "trough-guided dose adjustment."
    )
  ) +
  theme_bw()
```

The simulated band is not a reproduction of Figure 2: the real cohort's
doses were adjusted from the first trough on, so only the POD 2 trough
reflects the protocol dose. That day is checked against the observed median
(4.0 ng/mL, Table 2) and the paper's own accumulation-aware model prediction
(4.2 ng/mL, Supplementary Table S3). The protocol dose is a lower bound on what
was given (the four subjects of Table 8 received 0.04-0.07 mg/kg on POD 1), so
the simulated median is expected to sit below both. It sits lower still than
the 3.4 ng/mL a typical subject on the protocol dose would reach, because the
POD 2 trough depends non-linearly on the elimination rate constant, whose
log-scale variance on this occasion (IIV of CL/F and V/F together with the
OCC 1 IOV of 0.929) is large.

```{r pod2-check}
pod2_med <- troughs$p50[troughs$POD == 2]
pod2_med
# Structural check only: a dose, unit or clearance error moves the median
# several-fold. A 2-fold envelope keeps the bound about five standard errors
# of a 200-subject median (log-scale SD of the trough near 0.8) away from the
# simulated value, so it does not depend on the cohort draw.
stopifnot(pod2_med > 4.0 / 2, pod2_med < 4.2 * 2)
```

# NCA of the steady-state dosing interval

PKNCA is run on the typical-value steady-state profiles at the Table 7
doses, one per occasion. The paper reports no NCA; the reference for the
comparison table is the 10 ng/mL target trough that Table 7's doses were
derived to attain.

```{r pknca}
ev_ss <- ev7 |>
  dplyr::filter(evid == 1L) |>
  dplyr::bind_rows(
    ev7 |>
      dplyr::filter(evid == 0L) |>
      dplyr::select(-time) |>
      dplyr::cross_join(data.frame(time = seq(0, 12, by = 0.1)))
  ) |>
  dplyr::arrange(id, time, dplyr::desc(evid == 1L))

sim_ss <- rxode2::rxSolve(mod_typ, ev_ss,
  returnType = "data.frame",
  rtol = 1e-10, atol = 1e-12, ssRtol = 1e-10, ssAtol = 1e-12, maxsteps = 1e6,
  keep = "OCC"
)

conc_df <- sim_ss |>
  dplyr::filter(!is.na(Cc)) |>
  dplyr::mutate(occasion = paste0("OCC", OCC)) |>
  dplyr::select(id, occasion, time, Cc)
dose_df <- ev_ss |>
  dplyr::filter(evid == 1L) |>
  dplyr::mutate(occasion = paste0("OCC", OCC)) |>
  dplyr::select(id, occasion, time, amt)

conc_obj <- PKNCA::PKNCAconc(conc_df, Cc ~ time | occasion + id)
dose_obj <- PKNCA::PKNCAdose(dose_df, amt ~ time | occasion + id)
intervals <- data.frame(
  start = 0, end = 12,
  cmax = TRUE, tmax = TRUE, cmin = TRUE, auclast = TRUE, cav = TRUE
)
nca <- PKNCA::pk.nca(PKNCA::PKNCAdata(conc_obj, dose_obj, intervals = intervals))

reference <- data.frame(occasion = paste0("OCC", 1:6), cmin = 10)
nlmixr2lib::ncaComparisonTable(
  nca, reference,
  by = "occasion", params = "cmin",
  units = c(cmin = "ng/mL")
) |>
  knitr::kable(caption = "Steady-state trough at the Table 7 doses against the 10 ng/mL target.")

as.data.frame(nca) |>
  dplyr::filter(PPTESTCD %in% c("cmax", "tmax", "cmin", "auclast", "cav")) |>
  dplyr::select(occasion, PPTESTCD, PPORRES) |>
  tidyr::pivot_wider(names_from = PPTESTCD, values_from = PPORRES) |>
  dplyr::rename(
    Occasion = occasion, `Cmax (ng/mL)` = cmax, `Tmax (h)` = tmax,
    `Cmin (ng/mL)` = cmin, `AUC0-12 (ng*h/mL)` = auclast, `Cavg (ng/mL)` = cav
  ) |>
  knitr::kable(digits = 2, caption = "Typical-value steady-state NCA by occasion.")

cmin_nca <- as.data.frame(nca) |> dplyr::filter(PPTESTCD == "cmin")
stopifnot(nrow(cmin_nca) == 6, all(abs(cmin_nca$PPORRES / 10 - 1) < 0.015))
```

# Assumptions and deviations

* **Occasion of the POD 1 doses.** Tacrolimus starts on POD 1, before the
  first occasion (POD 2). The paper does not say which occasion its POD 1
  dosing records carried; they are given OCC = 1 here, so the POD 1
  clearance is the one the POD 2 trough informs. OCC outside 1-6 gives
  CL/F without IOV; the model was not fitted beyond POD 11.
* **Occasion boundaries.** In the virtual cohort a record's occasion follows
  its calendar postoperative day, switching at midnight. The paper defines
  occasions by postoperative day without giving the clock time of the switch.
* **Per-occasion IOV variances.** Each occasion carries its own estimated
  variance (Table 5); none is shared. The six IOV etas are selected by
  occasion indicators, so rxode2 reports that they are not mu-referenced.
  rxode2 has no occasion level for random effects, and the indicator form is
  how occasion-specific etas are expressed; the warning matters only for the
  speed of a future estimation run, not for simulation.
* **V/F of 123.9 L.** Table 4 prints 123.9 L and Equation 10 rounds it to
  124 L. The typical V/F values of Table 8 reproduce with 123.9 (e.g. 139.0 L
  at 24.6 months, against 139.1 L with 124), so 123.9 is used.
* **CL/F of 4.85 L/h is rounded.** The typical CL/F values of Table 7 are
  consistent with an unrounded estimate near 4.854 L/h (the OCC 1 row needs at
  least 4.854 to print 3.21, the OCC 5 row at most 4.854 to print 5.09). The
  printed 4.85 L/h is used; the gates above allow 0.5%.
* **Covariate units.** The paper models total bilirubin in mg/dL (reference
  2 mg/dL) and age in months (reference 12 months). The canonical covariate
  columns are `TBILI` in umol/L and `AGE` in years, so `model()` converts
  with 1 mg/dL = 17.1 umol/L and 12 months per year.
* **Signs of the clearance exponents.** Table 4 lists the bilirubin and AST
  exponents as positive numbers in a 'negative power' model; Equation 9 prints
  them as -0.353 and -0.106, which is how they are stored.
* **Combined residual error.** Equation 3 gives
  W = sqrt(add^2 + prop^2 * IPRED^2), which is the nlmixr2 default
  combined form with both components as standard deviations.
* **Virtual cohort.** Age, weight, bilirubin and AST distributions are
  approximations built from Table 1 and Table 7 summaries (see the cohort
  section); the real cohort's individual covariate trajectories and dosing
  histories are not published.
